amendments.rule: A pronominal suffix aligns to the English pronoun that realizes it, which is usually a possessive or object pronoun: `מִינֵהוּ` → *his kind* splits into the noun and *his*. **Where the ASV's paraphrase realizes one suffix twice, both pronouns belong to that suffix's one possibly discontinuous unit; an earlier realization does not make the later one `added`.** `מִכֶּם מָזוֹר` → *cure you of your wound* gives *you ... your* to the suffix and heads on *you*, the direct pronoun rather than the possessive recasting. **Where the ASV intensifies a possessive with *own*, the whole emphatic possessive belongs to the suffix:** `דְּרָכֶיךָ` → *thine own ways* gives *thine own* to the suffix and *ways* to the noun, headed on *thine*; do not attach *own* to the host noun merely because it stands beside it. **Where the ASV replaces the suffix's ordinary pronoun with a lexical nominal expression naming its referent, that whole expression realizes the suffix and the supplied lexical antecedent is not `added`; head on the noun or name that carries the referent.** `נְחָלֶיהָ` → *the streams of Edom* gives *of Edom* to the suffix and heads on *Edom*, and the suffix in `בִּסְעִיפֶיהָ הַפֹּרִיָּה` → *in the outmost branches of a fruitful tree* takes *of a tree*, headed on *tree*, while the adjective keeps *fruitful*. **An independent personal pronoun the ASV renders the same way goes with it.** Where a written subject or object pronoun is realized not by an English pronoun but by a demonstrative with a supplied lexical noun naming its referent, that whole expression realizes the pronoun and the supplied noun is not `added`; head on the noun carrying the referent: `הִיא הַסִּיר` → ***this city*** *is the caldron* gives *this city* to `הִיא`, exactly as rule 20's identifying formula gives *These ... that* to a `הוּא`, and an ASV italic on the supplied noun corroborates it without deciding it, by rule 7. Where the referent's own noun stands written in the clause, the pronoun takes only the determiner the ASV writes for it and the article is `unrepresented` under rule 41's limit: `הִיא נִתְּנָה הָאָרֶץ` → ***this*** *land* *is given*. **Where the ASV expands an object suffix into a full nominal expression containing a pronoun, the whole expression may realize the suffix, but the target head remains the pronoun that directly realizes the suffix's lexeme:** `אֲשִׁיבֶנּוּ` → *I will turn away the punishment thereof* gives *the punishment thereof* to the suffix and heads on *thereof*, not on the generic noun *punishment*. All eight occurrences of this prophetic formula across Amos 1–2 follow that analysis. Where no suffix or other possessive morpheme is present, a supplied possessive expression such as *your own* or *thine own* answers to no source morpheme and is `added` under rule 30. **The suffix on an infinitive construct is that infinitive's subject and takes the English subject pronoun the ASV writes for it**, while the infinitive keeps the verb: `עַד כַּלֹּתוֹ אֹתְךָ` → *until he have consumed thee* gives *he* to the suffix and *have consumed* to the infinitive, and the object marker and its own suffix are read separately by rules 16 and 11. The ASV's pronoun need not agree in number with the suffix — `עַד הַאֲבִידוֹ אֹתָךְ` → *until they have caused thee to perish* — because the English subject answers to the referent the translation has in view; align the pronoun that is written. This governs only a suffix that is actually present: where none is, a subject pronoun the ASV supplies for an infinitive belongs to the infinitive itself under rules 48 and 52, and rules 40 and 43 dispose of the other places where the English pronoun realizing a morpheme is neither possessive nor object.
amendments.why: Rule 18's lexical-antecedent clause is written for suffixes only, so a verse pass meeting an independent pronoun rendered by a supplied lexical noun has nothing to read but rule 30's `added`, and the ASV's italic invites exactly that. EZK.11 met it four times — הִיא → *this city* at 11.3, 11.7 and 11.11, and הִיא → *this* at 11.15 where הָאָרֶץ is written — and resolved all four the same way. The extension is small and already half-made inside the contract: rule 20's identifying-formula paragraph gives an independent `הוּא` an expanded English realization (*These ... that*), and rule 18's own נְחָלֶיהָ → *the streams of Edom* is the same reasoning for a suffix. The corpus does not contradict it; it aligns independent pronouns to determiners in 140 units headed on *that*. Adding it here rather than as a new rule keeps the qualification where a reader will land, and the second half of the clause ties the case back to rule 41's limit so the two are not read apart.

conventions: An independent הִיא with no noun written for it takes the ASV's whole supplied expression *this city* (11.3, 11.7, 11.11), headed on *city*: the pronoun names a referent and the italic *city* is what the ASV writes for that referent, so it is not `added` under rule 30's *no morpheme licenses it at all*. Where the referent's noun is written (11.15 הָאָרֶץ), the pronoun takes only the determiner *this* and the article is `unrepresented` under rule 41's limit. The competing reading, which leaves the pronoun a bare *this* and marks *city* `added`, is named in each verse's notes.

The Sp1cs suffix of אֲדֹנָי is `unrepresented` in all six occurrences of the divine title (11.7, 11.8, 11.13, 11.16, 11.17, 11.21): the ASV writes *the Lord*, never *my Lord*, and where a *the* is written it is the construct noun's supplied one under rule 29 — 11.13's vocative *Ah Lord Jehovah* writes none, so אֲדֹנָי there is bare. BSB represents this suffix, and the six-token disagreement is convention rather than error.

A resumptive element inside an אֲשֶׁר clause that the ASV renders with a single *where* is `unrepresented` rather than fused into the relative: שָׁם at 11.16 and בָּהֶם with its suffix at 11.17, on rule 22's first sentence, since *where* is the ordinary rendering of אֲשֶׁר by itself. Where the ASV does write a word for the resumptive preposition it takes it — 11.15's לָהֶם gives *unto* to the preposition beside *whom* on the relative, and only the suffix goes unrepresented. The corpus contains a contrary precedent, 1KI.17.19 fusing a non-contiguous אֲשֶׁר … שָׁם into one *where* unit under rule 35, which is why no rule was promoted; each verse's notes name it.

In the covenant and predicate formulas built on הָיָה לְ (11.11, 11.16, 11.20), the written הָיָה carries the copula under rules 17 and 21, so the predicative לְ before the predicate noun is `unrepresented` and rule 49's resultative frame has nothing left to attach; a dative or possessive לְ in the same clause is likewise `unrepresented` where the ASV recasts it as a bare possessive (*your caldron*, *my people*, *their God*), its suffix taking the possessive under rule 40, while the one the ASV spells out (*to them*, 11.16) goes to the preposition under rule 11.

Directive he is read off the ASV and not off the token: fused with its host into one English word at 11.1 קָדִימָה → *eastward*, 11.18 שָׁמָּה → *thither* and 11.22 מִלְמָעְלָה → *above* (rules 30, 32), but its own aligned unit at 11.24 כַשְׂדִּימָה, where the ASV writes *into* for it and *to* for the following אֶל. None of the four is treated as a paragogic he.

report: Checked all 49 candidate lemma groups and read the dump end to end. No genuine split: every multi-treatment bucket is the ASV writing different English in different contexts, licensed by the ASV or by MACULA's morphology. מִן → *from* beside *out of* inside 11.17 is what the ASV wrote; אֲדֹנָי is *the Lord* everywhere except the vocative *Ah Lord Jehovah* of 11.13; רָחַק heads on *far* in the light-verb *Get you far* (15) and on *removed* where *far off* is adverbial (16), which is one subtraction test giving two answers.

The article-and-construct family, the chapter's largest recurring risk, is uniform. A present article takes the phrase's single written *the* before a supplied one (11.1 הַקַּדְמוֹנִי, 11.19 הָאֶבֶן, rules 47 and 29); an arthrous rendering gives the construct a supplied *the* and the rectum's article its own (11.1, 11.12, 11.23); both articles of הָעִיר הַזֹּאת go unrepresented because the demonstrative is the only determiner written (11.2, 11.6), as does הָאָרֶץ's in 11.15 where הִיא carries *this*.

Audited the three `added` units by hand, since the candidate table is blind to them. *The time* (11.3) is rule 17's supplied lexical subject with no source nominal; *even* (11.15) and *as for them* (11.21) are the two limits rule 16 states in its own words — no marker stands on the appositive, and no marker or fronting לְ stands on the topicalized phrase, whose אֶל already has its own *after*. The converse holds too: every supplied word that was folded (*this city*, *are they*, *them of the captivity*, *with the slain*, *for a little while*, *did lift up*) has a morpheme licensing it under rules 18, 20, 33, 46 or 17.

Recast prepositions are consistent chapter-wide: a dative or possessive לְ goes unrepresented with its suffix taking the English pronoun (11.11, 11.17, 11.19, 11.20), an ASV-written *to them* goes to the preposition (11.16), and the predicative לְ of הָיָה לְ goes unrepresented in all three covenant clauses because הָיָה carries the copula (11.11, 11.16, 11.20). The fusions are consistent as well: לָכֵן (4, 7, 16, 17), מֵעַל → *from* (15, 23, 24), בְּקֶרֶב → *within* (19), לְעֻמַּת → *beside* with the copula (22), מִלְמַעְלָה → *above* (22), each meeting rule 30's one-English-word test, while the same מִן phrase spelled out in three English words at 11.1 is split by rule 2.

Ledger re-verified: unit counts per verse against the printed source and target totals in all 25 verses sum to 548, matching the validator, and no verse leaves an id unpartitioned or a head outside its unit.

BSB: no genuine error. All 34 disagreements are documented convention differences — the object marker (rule 16, ×7), the אֲדֹנָי suffix where the ASV writes *the Lord* and never *my Lord*, recast dative and predicative לְ (rule 40), לֵאמֹר's לְ (rule 27), resumptives after אֲשֶׁר, and an article standing under a demonstrative. The waw BSB represents at 11.17 is simply absent from the ASV, which opens *I will gather you* with no connective. Nothing was changed to move the rate.

One amendment offered, to rule 18, extending its lexical-antecedent clause from suffixes to independent pronouns: הִיא → *this city* at 11.3, 11.7 and 11.11, and → *this* at 11.15 where the noun is written. I did not promote the other candidate — a rule making a resumptive שָׁם or בָּהֶם unrepresented under a single *where* (11.16, 11.17) — because the corpus contradicts it: 1KI.17.19 fuses a non-contiguous אֲשֶׁר … שָׁם into one *where* unit. That reading is logged as a chapter convention with the competing precedent named, and stays out of the contract.
